statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns a result r, r equals the number of pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and lower <= nums[i] + nums[j] <= upper.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: For every nums, lower, and upper satisfying the preconditions, count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns a result r; it does not fail by overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(nums) * (len(nums) - 1) / 2.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, l1, u1) returns r1 and count_fair_pairs(nums, l2, u2) returns r2, r2 <= r1.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= l1 <= l2 <= u2 <= u1 <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r, count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, mid) returns r1, and count_fair_pairs(nums, mid + 1, upper) returns r2, we have r = r1 + r2.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; for an integer mid, -1000000000 <= lower <= mid < upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r and count_fair_pairs(nums', lower', upper') returns r', r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000. Let nums' be the slice with len(nums') = len(nums) and nums'[i] = -nums[i] for every i; let lower' = -upper and upper' = -lower.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r and count_fair_pairs(nums', lower, upper) returns r', r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000. Let nums' be a slice with the same length as nums that is a permutation of nums: there is a bijection p from {0,...,len(nums)-1} to itself with nums'[i] = nums[p(i)] for every i.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r, r > 0 if and only if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and lower <= nums[i] + nums[j] <= upper.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r, r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; len(nums) = 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r, if lower <= 2 * v <= upper then r = len(nums) * (len(nums) - 1) / 2, and otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000. There is an integer v such that nums[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r, r = len(nums) * (len(nums) - 1) / 2 if and only if for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), lower <= nums[i] + nums[j] <= upper.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower <= upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r and count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper - 1) returns r', r - r' equals the number of pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and nums[i] + nums[j] = upper.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower < upper <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever count_fair_pairs(nums, lower, upper) returns r and count_fair_pairs(nums, lower + 1, upper) returns r', r - r' equals the number of pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and nums[i] + nums[j] = lower.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; -1000000000 <= lower < upper <= 1000000000.
